t: Muslims believe the Quran was revealed orally to Muhammad through the angel Gabriel over some 23 years, from 610 CE, and was later compiled and given a standard text; modern scholars debate how and when its final form was fixed.
It has 114 chapters arranged roughly by decreasing length rather than in the order of revelation, and it is recited in Arabic in prayer, with the whole text memorised by those called hafiz.

Its meaning has been explained by centuries of commentary (tafsir), its text has been copied in many scripts and printed since the 16th century, and it has been translated into over a hundred languages.
dyk: Moses is named 136 times in the Quran, more often than any other individual, and Jesus is named more often than Muhammad is.
ev: According to Islamic tradition, Muhammad receives his first revelation in the Cave of Hira on the Laylat al-Qadr
Muhammad dies; Muslims hold that the revelation was complete by this year, and tradition says the Quran did not yet exist in book form
Caliph Uthman orders a committee headed by Zayd ibn Thabit to prepare a standard text, the Uthmanic codex, and sends copies to city centres
The date Gerd R. Puin gave to the Sanaa manuscripts, whose 12,000 pieces were found in a mosque in Yemen in 1972
The Baghdad scholar Ibn Mujahid establishes seven acceptable readings of the Quran
Robert of Ketton completes the first translation of the Quran into a Western language, Latin
The first complete Quran printed with movable type is produced in Venice, for the Ottoman market
Al-Azhar University publishes the Cairo edition, which standardises Quranic orthography and became the basis of later editions

f.made: Muslims hold that it is the speech of God, revealed to Muhammad through the angel Gabriel; according to tradition it was compiled under Abu Bakr and given a standard form under Uthman
f.form: Arabic text in 114 chapters (surahs) of verses (ayat); 6,236 verses in the Hafs reading; rhymed prose; one estimate counts 77,430 words
f.where: Read and recited worldwide; early manuscripts include the Sanaa fragments found in Yemen in 1972, and several digitised copies are held by the Cambridge University Digital Library
f.known: believed by Muslims to be God's own speech; recited in Arabic in prayer; 114 surahs opening with the Bismillah, except the ninth; seven readings fixed by Ibn Mujahid; tafsir commentary; calligraphy and illumination; the 1924 Cairo edition
